welcome.subtitle: A Human-AI Teaming Playground
welcome.desc: Explore how a human dispatcher and agentic AI can co-operate on the Flatland railway simulation.
welcome.doorsAria: How do you want to start?

introduction.title: Introduction
introduction.subtext: A guided tour. Modes, layout and environment are set for you.

build.title: Build your own
build.subtext: Choose the network, scenario and layout yourself.

experiments.title: Experiments
experiments.subtext: A prepared, reproducible condition: premade plan, chosen disturbances, study layout.

hint.gridCap: Capped here so a fresh session stays smooth on the hosted demo's free hardware. Need bigger? Session Properties → Basic goes up to {{max}}.
hint.maxSteps: Max simulation length. Higher = more thorough what-if forecasts but slower.
hint.grid: Capped for a smooth run on the hosted demo's free hardware — for a bigger grid or more trains, open Session Properties after starting a session (gear icon, Basic tab).

welcome.experimentsNote: First cut. Only scenarios that ship a premade plan are offered, so a run is reproducible. Participant ids and counterbalanced mode order are not built yet — that is the Experiment entity in the plan.
welcome.planNote: Plan — this scenario ships a premade plan. The trains follow it exactly from the first step; anything you override leaves the plan and is driven by the AI instead.

disturbances.hint: Scripted events that hit at fixed steps. Pick any combination — none is the undisturbed reference run.

summary.tour: You start the tour “{{name}}”: {{modes}}, about {{minutes}} min.

three-modes-original.name: Three modes · original layout
three-modes-original.description: The same conflict handled in all three modes — Recommendation, Co-Learning, Director — in the hardcoded default layout, with a short survey after each.

two-modes-guide-light.name: Two modes · Guide Mode Light
two-modes-guide-light.description: Recommendation and Co-Learning in the three-zone layout: left reports, centre shows the network, right decides. Same environment as the original tour, so the layout is the only difference.

director-only.name: Director only
director-only.description: Straight into the Director screen — strategy tiles, forecast, AI-activity feed — with no walk and no survey. For showing that screen on its own.

recommendation.title: Recommendation
recommendation.whatHappens: As trains run, the AI watches for conflicts. When one appears, it proposes a preferred solution with a confidence score.
recommendation.focusView: The map — you act on each conflict where it happens; the recommendation card on the right is the AI’s suggested fix.
recommendation.yourRole: You stay in charge — accept the AI’s suggestion, or choose differently yourself.

control.0: Accept or reject the AI’s suggested policy change
control.1: Override any individual train’s next decision yourself

watch.0: A recommendation card on the right, with a confidence % and countdown

recommendation.goal: Get all trains to their destination with as little delay as possible.

co-learning.title: Co-Learning
co-learning.tagline: Neutral options, you decide and reflect.
co-learning.whatHappens: Same kind of situation — but this time the AI doesn’t push a favorite. It lays out the options neutrally.
co-learning.focusView: The map — compare your own action (blue) against the AI’s plan (yellow) right where the trains run; the what-if compare on the right deepens it. Reflection opens separately when you’re ready.
co-learning.yourRole: You choose freely; every decision is recorded. Afterwards, you reflect on what you did — and get the AI’s perspective on it too.

control.0: Choose freely between neutral options — nothing is ranked for you
control.1: Override any individual train’s decision yourself
control.2: Trigger “Reflect now” at any point during the run

watch.0: No ranking or badges on the options
watch.1: A “Reflect now” option becomes available as you go, and opens on its own once a decision is resolved

co-learning.goal: Same task — but the focus here is what you learn about the situation, and about working with the AI.

director.title: Director
director.tagline: You set the goal, the AI acts.
director.whatHappens: You choose which objective the plan should pursue. The AI then dispatches every train on its own and re-plans as the situation changes.
director.focusView: The three strategy tiles above the map. “Auf Karte” draws the chosen plan onto the map as dashed routes, so you see what an objective changes before committing it.
director.yourRole: Supervise the objective, not the trains. You steer by changing what the plan optimises for.

control.0: Choose the objective: delay, connections, or stability
control.1: Preview it on the map, and replay it, before committing
control.2: Swap the dispatching policy in the toolbar
control.3: Pause, resume, or end the shift

watch.0: The AI-activity feed: what the planner decided, and when it re-planned
watch.1: The forecast: what the objective gives, and what it costs
watch.2: Dashed look-ahead routes on the map after a preview

director.goal: See how well the AI performs autonomously — and notice where you feel the pull to intervene.

legend.warning: Notice — keep an eye on it

finished.title: Episode finished
finished.message: All agents have reached their target.

scenarios.neutralHint: Options shown neutrally — compare and decide; none is marked “best”.

e1-station-hold.name: E1: stop after the crossing
e1-station-hold.description: E1 (WN→WAL) stands for 8 steps just after the crossing, with E2 following on the same track — the delay is passed straight on to the train behind.

0.label: E1: unscheduled stop (+8 steps)
0.description: E1 stops on the open line; E2 follows on the same track and inherits the delay.

w1-door-fault.name: W1: door fault in the single-track section
w1-door-fault.description: W1 (WAL→WN) stands for 8 steps while it occupies the single-track section, so both eastbound trains have to wait it out.

0.label: W1: door fault (+8 steps)
0.description: W1 blocks the single-track section; according to the plan, E1 and E2 are already waiting for the crossing.

e1-late-into-the-section.name: E1: +6 steps before the single-track section
e1-late-into-the-section.description: E1 stands for 6 steps at Weesen, exactly the headway the plan gives it over E2. It therefore reaches the single-track section at the same step E2 is planned to. Without it all three trains drive through the section non-stop; with it E2 has to give way in front of it, and W1 — timed to arrive just as E2 clears — is held at the eastern mouth too.

0.label: E1: unscheduled stop at WN (+6 steps)
0.description: E1 loses exactly the lead the timetable gives it over E2. Both now reach the single-track section in the same step; W1 follows third, as planned.

deadlock_avoidance.label: DLA (Default)
deadlock_avoidance.description: Avoids deadlocks proactively by checking opponent paths.

shortest_path.label: Shortest Path
shortest_path.description: Each agent picks the action that minimises distance to its target.

random.label: Random
random.description: Picks a random valid action per agent.

goal_directed.label: Director Planner
goal_directed.description: Plans all trains with the weighted model-guided search (punctuality / connections / stability), then drives the plan.

plan.label: Scripted Plan
plan.description: Drives every train along the scenario's premade plan; trains the plan does not cover, or that the operator overrode, fall back to deadlock avoidance.

train.name: Train {{n}}
train.conflictsOnlyTitle: Trains caught in a conflict (blocked, blocking or disrupted)
train.myOverride: Your override — click again to clear it
train.setOverride: Set as override for this train
train.aiRecommendation: The AI’s recommendation for this train

roster.title: Agents
roster.overrideOnRight: Set overrides in the train detail on the right
roster.redHint: red = your override · click again to clear it
roster.slackTooltip: {{n}} step(s) of slack before the latest arrival ({{target}})

table.title: Trains — disposition table

hint.recommended: ★ = the AI’s recommendation for this train · red = your override
hint.neutral: Options are equal — you decide first · red = your override

table.emptyConflicts: No train is in a conflict right now.

item.trainText: the colour identifies the train, the same in the list, on the map and in the time–distance diagram
item.decisionText: next decision point; the pills beside it are the actions you can pick (the same as in the train list)

legend.scoreText: = outcome quality of the option (weighted KPIs)
legend.confidenceBefore: = how sure the AI is that the option beats the

note.mock: Demo data — no real comparison run behind it.
note.uncalibrated: The AI’s model value, not calibrated against observed outcomes.
note.equal: on a par with the current course
note.priorOnly: {{lead}} — no comparison variants, so the evidence is weak.
note.spreadMedium: the variants lie moderately far apart

why.heading: Why this option
why.connectionsDetail: More trains complete than under the current plan.
why.delayDetail: Mean delay stays at or below the current plan.

colearning.withPrefs: Takes {{n}} confirmed preference(s) into account — a ranking nudge, not a hard rule.
colearning.noPrefs: Ranking still rests purely on the KPI assessment (no confirmed preferences yet).

preview.hintPinned: The reroute stays visible on the track diagram & ZWL
preview.hintHover: Hovering shows the changed route on the track diagram & ZWL

inspector.noSelectionText: Hover over a train or select one on the track diagram or in the train list.
inspector.noSelectionHint: It then shows position, destination, status and the actions available.

log.titleTooltip: Every decision this session: who decided, when, how long it took, accepted or overridden.
log.directorNote: You intervened {{n}}×: exceptions to an autonomous operation.
log.empty: No decisions in this session yet.
log.aiSuggestionTitle: The AI’s suggestion at the time of the decision

rationale.title: Why this decision?
rationale.hint: “Just this once” stays a one-off decision and does not become a rule.

effect.calloutBefore: Because you confirmed that, I now weight
effect.note: A ranking nudge, not a hard rule.
effect.applied: Applied — the planner recomputes with it.
effect.onlyDeliberate: Only deliberate decisions count — quick approvals stay out.

impact.titleTooltip: Trains whose route is blocked by another train’s malfunction before it clears — not the disrupted trains themselves (those are in Events).
impact.empty: No train is affected right now.
impact.heldText: — for your decision. The rest of the network keeps running.
impact.summaryOne: One train affected · one measure needed
impact.blockedByShort: blocked by {{train}} at ({{row}}, {{col}}) · reaches it in {{eta}} · clears in {{clears}}
impact.bufferNone: none — the train would stand for {{n}} steps
impact.countdown: AI decides in {{n}}s if you don’t

reflection.title: Co-Learning Reflection
reflection.calmNudgeTitle: Things have calmed down — a good moment to reflect
reflection.momentNote: Picked from {{n}} decisions — by pattern break, override and handover to the AI.

q.cuesIntervened: You intervened {{n}} time(s). Which signals made you step in?
q.cuesNone: You let the AI run without intervening. Which signals were you watching?
q.expected: Where did the outcome differ from what you expected — and why?
q.rule: What if-then rule would you draw for a similar situation next time?
q.trust: When did you trust the AI, and when did you override it? What drove that?
q.success: How would you measure whether this run went well?

whatif.titleTooltip: Formulate your own action for the selected train and compare its simulated future with the AI’s plan.
whatif.empty: Select a train (track diagram, list or impact) to compare your plan against the AI.
whatif.failed: Could not simulate this branch. Try another action.
whatif.committed: ✓ My plan committed as an override.
whatif.readonly: Read-only in Director — the AI keeps actuation.

note.recommendation: Compare your action against the AI’s current course.
note.coLearning: Formulate your own action and compare it with the AI — neither is marked “right”.
note.director: Supervisory what-if — inspect a branch; the AI keeps actuation under the directive.

forecast.title: Effect over the next 30 minutes
forecast.horizonShort: Reliable only to {{horizon}} · {{problems}} open problem(s) — more open problems make the future less certain
forecast.noteLong: Rule-based projection from this option’s KPI deltas — the next 30 minutes are not re-simulated.
forecast.emptyText: Pick an option in the strategy widget (“On the map” or “Take it”) to see its forecast.

directive.endShiftTitle: Ends the shift and shows the review — you can go back.

aiActivity.title: What the AI is doing
aiActivity.empty: No planner decisions yet. Start the autonomous run — then this says what the AI decides and when it re-plans.
aiActivity.keptRejected: {{reason}}: plan kept — the simulation rejected the change
aiActivity.keptNotBetter: {{reason}}: plan kept (the change was no better)

strategyReflection.title: Your decision
strategyReflection.noPrice: With no measurable price on the other axes.
strategyReflection.contradiction: So far you have mostly prioritised {{was}}, here {{now}}. Was that this situation — or should I change my assumption about you?
strategyReflection.guard: “Just this once” deliberately does not become a rule — a situational decision should not turn into a lasting preference.

punctuality.title: Minimise delay
punctuality.goal: Trains to their destination as early as possible — running time before waiting.

connections.title: Keep connections
connections.goal: Secure transfers — trains wait for them.

stability.title: Maximise stability
stability.goal: Keep reserve in the network — robust against the next disruption.

strategy.title: Choose a strategy
strategy.subtitle: Which goal should the autonomous plan pursue?
strategy.simulatingNote: Two whole episodes are played out (carry on as before vs. this goal, same disruptions) — about 7 s.
strategy.noForecast: No forecast: {{reason}} — the tiles still take effect, they set the planner’s goals.
strategy.firstPlan: The first plan is being computed (about 10 s) — then the three strategies.
strategy.planningNote: Each strategy is planned in full (three variants, about 20 s, on copies) — the running session is untouched. You can apply one already.
strategy.waitingForPause: I compute the forecast as soon as you pause — it takes about 20 s, and while the run moves it would already be out of date on arrival. You can apply a goal at any time.
strategy.allAgree: All three goals lead to the same plan here — no train is weighing them against each other right now. The choice takes effect at the next conflict.
strategy.preferred: Fits the preference you taught me — {{why}}. A suggestion, not a preselection.
strategy.unchanged: Runs every train like the current plan.
strategy.holds: {{n}} wait instead of taking another route.
strategy.fellBackTo: The planner takes {{plan}} here — the search found nothing better.
strategy.replayedTitle: Replayed to the end of the episode (from step {{step}})
strategy.changesNothing: The planner stays with the running plan — this goal changes nothing here.
strategy.contradicts: Careful: the simulation contradicts the assessment above. The models judge rerouted paths too optimistically — when in doubt, the replay counts.
strategy.simTitle: Plays this variant and the running one to the end of the episode (about 7 s) and compares the result.
strategy.simFailed: The simulation failed — the model values above stand.
strategy.planFailed: The strategies could not be planned.
strategy.previewUnchanged: This goal runs every train like the current plan — the click shows that plan.
strategy.previewPause: Pause the run — then the reroute is computed and can be clicked here.
strategy.previewNoPlan: First “Compute options” — without a plan there is no route to show.
strategy.previewNoRoute: No route is available for this goal.
strategy.directPlan: the direct line plan (no conflict handling)
strategy.avoidancePlan: the avoidance plan (conflicts routed around, no search)
strategy.hypothesisCost: When goals conflict, you prioritise {{goal}} — even when it costs {{cost}}.

shift.title: Shift review
shift.subtitle: {{arrived}}/{{total}} trains at their destination ({{pct}} %)
shift.unattended: You set no goal in this shift — the AI ran on the initial directive throughout. So there is nothing I could learn about your priorities either.
shift.replayBefore: On a fresh copy of the same episode — same tracks, same timetable, same disruptions — the plan gives {{delay}} delay,
shift.notAllArrived: not all trains at their destination
shift.predicted: The models had put connections at {{pct}} % — the search value is a capped geometric mean and deliberately lower than the share that counts.
shift.replayNote: What is replayed is the plan applied last, from step 0. That says “what this plan achieves on this episode” — not “this is how the shift went”, because it was re-planned along the way.
shift.noNewCarried: You confirmed no new preference in this shift. From earlier shifts, this still applies:
shift.noneConfirmed: No confirmed preference yet. Without a confirmed rule the ranking rests purely on the KPI assessment — I add no guesses.
shift.patternCarried: Pattern: {{label}} ({{pct}} % of {{n}} deliberate decisions from earlier shifts)
shift.weightsAfter: They count as a suggestion, not as a rule.
shift.oneOffs: You marked {{n}} decision(s) as a one-off. I did not learn those — that is exactly what the option is for.
shift.contradiction: You prioritised {{first}} {{firstCount}}× and {{second}} {{secondCount}}×. What was different about the situation — or does it depend on something I do not know yet?
shift.nothingToCarry: There is nothing to carry over: without a deliberate decision in this shift I have no evidence to take along.
shift.saved: ✓ Saved. From the next shift on, your preferences are a starting suggestion — profile from {{n}} completed shift(s). The matching tile is marked there; it is not set automatically.
shift.saveError: Saving did not work. Nothing was carried over — the next shift starts unchanged.
shift.canCarry: {{n}} goal decision(s) from this shift can go into your long-term profile
shift.firstOne: — so far this is your first.
shift.save: Save preferences for the next shift
shift.saveNote: What is carried over is the counted evidence and the confirmed rules. One-offs (“just this once”) and passive approvals stay out. Without a click the next shift starts cold.
shift.method: Rule-based review from this shift’s decision log — no language model, no interpretation beyond the numbers shown.
